intention: host.py refuses a non-final answer BY NAME, at _post, before the meter is ever asked. A non-streaming request that comes back with `done` not true got no answer at all, and today that fact reaches the caller wearing HostUnmetered's face.
why: MEASURED 2026-08-18T06:35Z against hex, after a night in which the WRONG explanation of this same failure was written into an append-only history. Unload qwen3-coder:30b (keep_alive 0, /api/ps empty), then fire four identical non-streaming /api/chat requests: every one returns HTTP 200 carrying 96 bytes — {"model":"","created_at":"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z","message":{"role":"","content":""},"done":false} — at 14.2s, 0.1s, 0.1s, 0.1s, while /api/ps shows the model resident afterwards. Minutes later, six consecutive requests succeed at 0.2-8.9s across num_ctx 8192/32768/81920. host.py sees that body and passes it through THREE checks: _post's status branch (200 is not >=400), _post's error-key branch (there is no 'error' key), and the chat branch's shape check (message IS a dict and its content IS a str — the empty string is one). It dies at the fourth, metered_cost, which refuses with a sentence about missing token counters. The counters are missing because nothing was evaluated; nothing was evaluated because the answer was never final. THE LIVED SYMPTOM: the aider_shim apprentice's first live fire died this way, and the error pointed at the meter, so the diagnosis went to the meter, to the counters, to ollama's omitempty, and finally to a timeout that was never involved — and that false chain now stands permanently in cairn/devices/aider_shim/history.json, because history is append-only. Law 7 says an error at a diagnostic surface must be loud; loud at the wrong organ costs more than silence, because it is followed.
how: One predicate at the chokepoint all three verbs already pass through. In _post, after the status and error-key branches and before the body is returned: if the request was non-streaming and the response's `done` is not True, raise a named error saying the host answered but had not finished (carrying the endpoint, the path, the model asked for, and the body verbatim — complete-diagnostic-on-first-pass). Put it in _post rather than in the chat branch so the two verbs whose behaviour under this condition is UNMEASURED are covered by construction rather than by a claim measured once on chat. No retry, no wait-for-load: that is a policy nobody has asked for, and build-minimal says it grows against a measured need.
traces_to: Law 7 (errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces and permanent in records of truth — this is the 'loud at the RIGHT surface' half), Law 3 (the failure's cause is a measurement, and tonight it was inferred instead), Law 10 (nothing here is immeasurable: one unload and four requests settled a question two days of prose could not).
gates: code-seam invariant, transcribed: PROVED + feeds-back-to-origin-on-failure (Laws 3 + 8). PROVE GATE: the tester runs proofs beside cairn/devices/inference_domain/ under isolation=netns, with a tooth that feeds the VERBATIM 96-byte body measured 2026-08-18T06:35Z through the real _post and asserts the raise names the non-final answer, plus a tooth that feeds a real successful body from the same session and asserts it passes untouched. THE HOLLOW-BUILD TRAP HAS A NAME HERE: a tooth that merely asserts 'some error is raised' goes green against HEAD, because HEAD already raises — HostUnmetered, from one layer further in. So at least one tooth must assert the ERROR TYPE and must red on HEAD. FEEDBACK-TO-ORIGIN: the origin is this module's own shape checks — a frame that passed three of them and died at the meter is a shape check that did not cover its surface — and the route back is a proof beside host.py, never a caller-side guard in aider_shim. ENTRY GATE at BUILDME: chart claim + intent_berth + sorted_berth. EMISSION GATE on WATCHME: the probe below armed at its berth or WatchmeEmissionRed. CLEARANCE into PROVED: harbor_master.clearance.clear.
falsifier: FALSIFIER: DONE when a response whose 'done' is not true on a non-streaming request is refused by a named error before metered_cost is reached, proved by a tooth that feeds the exact 96-byte body measured tonight and asserts the raise names the non-final answer — and reds against HEAD, where that body raises HostUnmetered instead. WRONG-INTENT if a real host is found that returns done:false on a complete non-streaming answer (which would make the predicate reject good work), or if the refusal fires on any of tonight's six good responses. HORIZON: the next cold-hex drive of the aider_shim apprentice — the exact event that produced the misdiagnosis — and no later than the next voyage that dials inference at all.
horizon: the next cold-hex drive of the aider_shim apprentice — the exact event that produced the misdiagnosis — and no later than the next voyage that dials inference at all
children: none, because the change is one predicate at one chokepoint (_post, which all three verbs call) plus its proofs; the two things it could have been split into — the refusal and a retry-until-loaded — are not siblings, because the retry is a policy question nobody has asked for and build-minimal says the refusal comes first and the retry grows against a measured need.

watchme.trigger: each ask recorded by inference_domain — the probe reads the domain's own ask log, so it fires on the traffic that already exists rather than on a clock
watchme.enough: enough when the refusal has fired at least once on live traffic AND no successful ask in the same log was ever refused by it — a guard that has never bitten is unproven, and a guard that bites a good answer is worse than the fault it replaced
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier: the count of non-final refusals, the count of good asks passed, and the count of HostUnmetered raised after the change (which should be raised only by genuinely counterless FINAL answers)
watchme.consumer: whoever next debugs a failed drive — the misdiagnosis this ticket exists to stop cost one voyage a false sentence in an append-only history

distinctions_recorded: THE 200 IS NOT A LIE AND MUST NOT BE TREATED AS ONE. ollama answers 200 because the request was accepted and the stream was opened; the frame is a legitimate non-final chunk that a STREAMING client would read and keep reading. The defect is entirely on our side: we asked for stream:False and then read a non-final frame as if it were the answer. A future reader tempted to file this as 'hex is broken' should read the raw body — it says done:false, which is exactly what it means.

num_ctx IS NOT THE DISCRIMINATOR AND NEITHER IS THE TIMEOUT — both were live hypotheses tonight and both are dead. Six consecutive successes at num_ctx 8192, 32768 and 81920 once the model is up; the empty frame arrives in 0.1s against a 120.0s bound, three orders of magnitude inside it, and the transport never raised. Recorded because both are the obvious next guesses and re-deriving a settled answer is Law 1's defect.

THE CHECK GOES AT _post, NOT IN THE CHAT BRANCH, AND THE REASON IS ABOUT EVIDENCE RATHER THAN TIDINESS. The empty frame was measured on /api/chat only, n=6. Whether /api/generate does the same while loading is unmeasured. A per-branch fix would be three copies of a claim measured once; the chokepoint fix keys on a property of the RESPONSE that holds for any verb, so the unmeasured verbs are covered without pretending they were measured.

host.py's validated_messages docstring says 'On Hex a cold qwen3-coder:30b load is ~18s (measured 2026-08-16)'. Tonight's cold load-and-answer at num_ctx 81920 measured 131.5s total_duration (load_duration 132ms, prompt_eval 468ms, eval 314ms — the balance is KV allocation). The docstring does not record what num_ctx its 18s was taken at, which is the defect in it: a measurement stored without the parameter it depends on becomes folklore the moment the parameter moves. Not fixed by this ticket; named so the next reader does not trust the 18s.

distinctions: THE PREDICATE IS `"done" in body and body["done"] is not True` — PRESENT and not true. The obvious `body.get("done") is not True` would refuse every embedding this system takes: real /api/embed responses carry no `done` key at all. The regression tooth that stands between the two forms was written FIRST, was green on HEAD, and its whole value is that it stayed green after.

THE COLD-LOAD DISCRIMINATOR, AND IT FALSIFIES A CLAIM THIS TICKET'S OWN `why` CARRIES. The frame needs COLD LOAD *AND* a large num_ctx (81920). Cold with the resolver's default options answers in ~2s and does not reproduce it; warm at any num_ctx does not reproduce it. The earlier 'num_ctx is NOT the discriminator' was measured WARM — the wrong condition. Same family as the timeout story this ticket was born to correct: a measurement taken under the wrong condition standing in for the one that matters. 'ps empty' is not the discriminator either: unload, poll /api/ps to [], ask with default options — answered cleanly at 1.9s.

THE ORDER WAS EVIDENCE-BEFORE-ASSERTION AND DELIBERATELY INVERTED CHEAP-FIRST. HEAD already raised on the 96-byte frame, so a tooth asserting merely 'some error' would be green on a codebase with no fix in it. The discriminating tooth asserts the TYPE, and was measured RED on HEAD through the _refuses helper's WRONG-TYPE branch — naming HostUnmetered where HostNonFinal was expected — never 'NO REFUSAL AT ALL'. That distinction is what the pre-fix run was FOR.

LIVE FIRE, BOTH HALVES, THROUGH THE REAL RESOLVER. Cold hex: 4 asks, 4 HostNonFinal carrying the frame verbatim, zero HostUnmetered. Warm: 8 answers at cost 17, zero refusals. Plus 9 asks at default options, all answered. AND THE FIRST WARM CONTROL WAS MISLABELLED BY ME: I called a still-loading host warm on elapsed wall-clock and read 8 refusals as 8 answers. The method changed — warmth is now established by OBSERVATION (retry until an ask actually answers), never by a clock.

THE WATCHME SPEC WAS UNBUILDABLE AS WRITTEN, and this is the finding to carry forward. Its `enough` counts refusals from the domain's own ask log. Measured at build time: domain.resolve writes the inference_calls row only AFTER resolver(request) RETURNS, so a raise leaves NO ROW — refusals are invisible to that log. Clause one (the refusal has fired on live traffic) was satisfied AT BIRTH by the live fire, n=4, and is recorded in the verdict rather than re-measured by a probe that would have to dial the host on a clock. The armed probe watches the fault RETURNING instead: a post-era chat row with no text AND zero cost is a non-final frame that got past _post and was CACHED — worse than the misdiagnosis this ticket started from, because it stops being an error at all and is served to every future asker of that canonical question. One is the finding; the clear needs 20 clean post-era chat rows. Logging refusals in domain.py is outside constrain's `in` list — ticket owed, not a silent widening.

TWO AUTHORED EXPECTATIONS CORRECTED INSIDE THEIR OWN DISPOSITIONS. (a) The predicate sits AFTER the not-a-dict guard, not before its successors as hypothesize wrote — it must, because it subscripts body; the behavioural half of that expectation held exactly, the positional half was written before the code was read. (b) '5 green validations to 6' is FALSE: the validation store keeps ONE CURRENT RECORD PER PROOF (ticket a-validation-is-one-current-record-not-a-trail), so the seal REPLACED test_host.json's 2026-08-17 record and the component stands at 5 validation files before and after. The prior record is in git one commit back, exactly where that design puts it.

THE SEAL'S HORIZON CLOSED MID-VOYAGE AND THE HARBOR CAUGHT IT — physics working, worth recording as a pass rather than a nuisance. Arming the probe changed the component's source fingerprint (449077209f18… -> 86c7b5b41a30…) after test_host.py had been sealed, and clearance.clear refused PROVED onto code that had moved under its proof.
